Q2.Q2D_counterfactual: The section's if_it_were_true consequence does not follow from D's wording. D says the four labels denote one kind of double, differing by the name declared in the test class. Renaming a variable does not, by itself, turn a Map repository into interaction verification; that example is a non sequitur and adds an unsupported consequence. It is also mismatched to the actual wording: D's proposed collapse concerns kinds of test double, whereas the rebuttal shifts to the Map implementation's role. Correct the section or remove that counterfactual; retain the valid explanation that roles depend on behavior/assertions, not merely a variable name. This is a LINKAGE/SECTIONS defect, not an SFPL finding.

Q6.form_and_objects: All are single sentences, roughly 114–123 characters and 15–16 whitespace words. A and D compare both objects; C names both and asserts same defaults; B only states a spy-stubbing recommendation and does not name mock. All are ordinary prose; B's `поскольку` provides a causal construction, while no option has a uniquely complex list or code format.
Q6.sfpl_revised: UNVERIFIED / counts show close lengths, same sentence count, and comparable prose. B's off-axis answer is an ANSC/coverage defect already recorded; do not relabel it as SFPL solely because it omits the mock comparison.
Q6.Q6B_what_actually: Its categorical wording is too broad: Java evaluates the invocation inside `when(spy.method())`, and an unstubbed concrete spy method generally executes. But a method already stubbed may return the prior stub without its real body; an abstract method has no real implementation to execute. Safer section text: «При `when(spy.method()).thenReturn(...)` Java сначала вызывает метод для подготовки stubbing. У незастаббированного конкретного метода spy выполняется реальная реализация; уже застаббированный метод или абстрактный метод не гарантирует такого вызова. Для подавления опасного реального вызова используй `doReturn(...).when(spy).method()`.» This narrows a genuine fact/linkage defect; does not change the prior ANSC finding that option B itself is off-axis.
Q6.Q6B_if_it_were_true: No. The hypothesis “doReturn starts the real method” does not logically entail “when is safe”; the two stubbing forms could both call real code, both avoid it, or differ. The section's present «Тогда настройка spy была бы безопасной» is not entailed by B's stated proposition, so it is a non sequitur. It also does not supply a useful counterexample to B's claim. Replace with a direct contrast: «Если бы `doReturn` запускал реальный метод, он не устранял бы побочный вызов при настройке; однако `doReturn(...).when(spy).method()` позволяет настроить ответ без такого вызова, тогда как `when(spy.method())` может вызвать доступную реальную реализацию.»
